start_here_runtime: 57 minutes with the full response; 55–60 with normal variation. The manuscript is 6,810 words at about 120 words per minute.
start_here_cut: If you have 50 minutes: Introduction to 4, Movement 1 to 6, Movement 2 to 7, Movement 3 to 7, Movement 4 to 7, Movement 5 to 6, Application to 5. Keep 37:3–5, 37:8–10, the ruach wordplay, 37:11–14, Ephesians 2:1–10, and the empty tomb.
start_here_guardrails: Do not reduce the vision to a metaphor for discouragement. The bones are Israel in exile, and the language reaches to the final resurrection.
Keep the primary referent: the return from Babylon. Do not claim Ezekiel 37 directly predicts the resurrection of Jesus without showing the canonical steps.
Do not merge “son of man” in Ezekiel with Daniel 7 or with Jesus’ title without noting the difference.
Do not promise every valley will end on your timetable. The text promises God can raise the dead, not that every prayer resolves quickly.
The gospel must be explicit: the cross, the empty tomb, and the Spirit. Do not end on “try harder.”
Keep the care note for grief, depression, and suicidal thoughts; safety comes before application.
start_here_evidence: The dry bones, the two-stage animation, the ruach wordplay, and the promise of opened graves are doing theological work, and the cross and the empty tomb are the turn.

slides.label: 01 · THE BIG IDEA
slides.note: The bones do not try. God speaks, and the dead live.

slides.label: 02 · THE VALLEY
slides.headline: The ground was covered with bones.

slides.label: 04 · THE WORD
slides.headline: God speaks to what cannot hear.
slides.big_sub: The dead live because He speaks.
slides.body: The prophet supplies the voice, not the life. Bone comes to bone, sinew to sinew, flesh to flesh, skin to skin. Then the valley goes quiet: the body is assembled, but there is no breath.
slides.pullquote: “O dry bones, hear the word of the LORD.”
slides.footline: The word builds a body. Only the Spirit gives breath.

slides.label: 05 · THE PAUSE
slides.headline: Is an assembled body alive?
slides.quote: “We have the structure. Isn’t that enough?”
slides.aside1: The bones came together. There was no breath in them.
slides.footline: Do not settle for bones in order.

slides.label: 06 · THE SPIRIT
slides.footline: The Spirit turns a graveyard into an army.

slides.label: 07 · THE PROMISE
slides.banner_main: “I will put my Spirit within you, and you shall live, and I will place you in your own land.”
slides.footline: The graves open because God keeps His word.

slides.label: 08 · THE GREATER RESURRECTION
slides.banner_main: “Even when we were dead in our trespasses, God made us alive together with Christ.”
slides.footline: The empty tomb is the guarantee.
